newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors planning union crackdown.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors planning union crackdown.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors are planning legal action against union leaders who have crippled key industries with strikes that the government has declared unlawful, a prosecution official said on Monday.
Domestic media reported that arrests of union leaders were imminent, but the official said no final decision had been made on what action to take.

"We are planning legal action, whatever that may be, within this week," said an official at the Seoul District Prosecutor's Office, who declined to be identified. "But the prosecution is still working out the details."
Yonhap Television News reported that prosecutors would seek arrest warrants for 50 union leaders.
Strikes began on December 26 after the government pushed a new labour bill through parliament in a six-minute dawn session with no debate and no opposition deputies present.
Unions are demanding repeal of the law. On Monday, workers resumed stoppages that have paralysed large sections of industry, including carmaking and shipbuilding.
